qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Long-term B2B chocolate outsourcing contracts feature cost-plus pricing mechanisms, but fail to absorb working capital financing shocks during commodity cycles; reported GAAP ROIC is chronically sub-12% (10-12% historically, plunging below 8% during cocoa surges).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Cost-plus chocolate outsourcing model cannot insulate against working-capital financing spikes when cocoa prices surge. Ballooning inventory drove Net Debt/EBITDA to 6.5x and forced volume contraction (-6.8% in FY25), keeping full-cycle ROIC well below the 12% threshold.
qualitative.evidence: Historically, reported GAAP ROIC hovered around 10.3%-13.1% (median ~11.5%), falling below the 12% hurdle. During the 2024-2025 cocoa price spike, working capital absorbed billions, sending H1 free cash flow to -CHF 2.1B and Net Debt/EBITDA to 6.5x. Recurring net profit dropped 36% due to surge in financing costs and volume fell 6.8%, proving lack of true pricing power across the business cycle.
